a pitch, from inside the current cohort

Hi Andrew, Liam, and Priya — I'd love to TA your next cohort.

Just wanted to make my case properly, so I built you a page :)
I'm Jennifer — software engineer, community + education enthusiast, and newly AI-empowered builder.

01why i want this

The class gave me a space. I want to keep it going.

The biggest thing this class gave me wasn't a tool or a technique — it was dedicated space, time, and community for working with this scary AI stuff. That's the part I'd love to help foster for the next cohort.

I went through an up-and-down journey with AI doom before landing somewhere genuinely optimistic, through this class. And as a woman software engineer learning new tech, I've held both feelings at once: very qualified, and very much an imposter. Funny how those two can coexist, right?

Things you don't understand can scare you. But if you work with them, they get less scary — and you start to see what they can do for you, rather than take from you.

This was my motivation for taking your class, and it's why I believe in what you are building: techno-optimism, learned through community. I'd love to help support folks who are sitting in the scared part right now, because I know exactly what that feels like.

02the evidence

I've been helping out already!

Technical help

  • Helped a classmate turn a prompt-driven data workflow into a saved, rerunnable script — moving the AI from runtime to build time, so it's cheaper and deterministic
  • Shared how to make a progressive web app you can install to your phone, and where to find free hosting
  • Showed folks how to ask the agent for automated regression tests so old bugs stay fixed

Community

  • Frequently shared resources and events in Discord — Matt Pocock's engineering skill library, Rundown AI's community bulletin board, Zo Computer's community vibe-coding event
  • I genuinely enjoy talking with people about their projects — and about their relationship with AI

Engineering wisdom

  • Taught classmates about GitHub
  • Shared eng pitfalls for classmates: scope bloat, and too much planning without enough building & iterating
  • Tried out classmates' projects and gave hands-on user-testing feedback

Since the cohort has many students who've never written code, having more engineers on call fills a real gap — the kind of debugging that unblocks someone in five minutes instead of derailing their whole week.

03proof i ship

Built weekly, demoed Saturdays, live now.

My main interests are around productivity, visualization, and AI agent workflows. In addition to finding and building my own tools, I also built trackers for the cost and carbon of my own AI use (two of the projects below), because the operational and environmental impact of this work matters to me. I also make creative passion projects!

Todo Now

daily driver

A personalized to-do PWA that lives on my phone — built to track and prioritize tasks across all areas of my life that works for my brain.

live site →

In-page Bug Reporter + auto-triage

built into Todo Now

A bug reporter built right into my todo app — shake my phone (or ⌘⇧P on desktop) to enter Report Mode, tap the elements involved, and the report files itself as a GitHub issue at the source, instead of getting lost in a notes app. A GitHub Actions automation then triages the issues and fixes the bugs automatically.

github →

AI Carbon Footprint

accelerator build

What does an everyday AI activity cost the planet? Preset scenarios translated into energy, carbon, and familiar equivalents — every number cited, with uncertainty bands.

live site →

AI Spend Tracker

accelerator build

Tracks what my AI coding agents actually cost per session across tools — multi-source ingest into a local store, priced at API-equivalent value, synced to a private dashboard.

github →

Flight → Google Calendar

chrome extension

A simple regex and local LLM-backed tool that takes flight confirmations in Gmail, then adds the trip to Google Calendar in one click.

github →

Ravenwood Rush

co-op browser game

A Wizard101-themed co-op minigame that runs right in the browser — restore Bartleby's wards before the shadow falls! Peer-to-peer multiplayer over PeerJS, canvas rendering, and no build step. Built purely for fun, with the same TDD-with-agents workflow as everything else.

private repo (for now)
04what i took away

The class changed how I build — here's the trail it left.

I've collected my favorite skills, keep running docs on agents and MCP servers, and practiced test-driven development.

  • ·Got flexible across workflows — using skills systematically to streamline my engineering flows and reduce review burnout, and using the same tools creatively — prototyping passion projects, or running /grill-me as a research interview.
  • ·Created my harness — a web-config repo, parallel role sessions, test-driven development with agents, and my own running docs on agents and MCP servers. I love that I can apply structured engineering practices to AI development!
  • ·Compiled a personal skills library — github.com/j-alicia-long/skill-library — portable AI skills that work across tools and projects. My favorites include Matt Pocock's /grill-me and /tdd, Emil Kowalski's animation & design, and /i-have-adhd.
  • ·Feeling a lot more organized — and inspired to build!
05the role

What I'd actually do, week to week.

  • a.Async-first responder on Discord — helping answer questions and unblock student projects. Assist live in class when my schedule allows.
  • b.Coach students on best practices — how to align on an idea with your agent, how to find the right tools for your goals, and how to just start building.
  • c.More structure in class comms — polls, sharing threads, celebrating small wins. The community improves the class experience, and a little scaffolding makes it even easier for quieter folks to join in.
  • d.Share the journey itself — the doom-to-empowered arc, the imposter feelings, and what changed. Sometimes the most useful thing a TA can say is "I felt that too, and here's what helped."
~2–3 hrs/week, alongside my day job
06the ask

Can we make this official?

If this sounds helpful, I'd love to talk about what a TA role could look like for the next cohort, or how we can put together a small group of volunteer TAs together.

Either way, I'd love to be able to continue participating in this community and having conversations with y'all about the crazy, exciting times we live in.

Thank you all for building this class. It changed how I work!

Thanks so much,
